ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 7.7%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 58.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 11.7%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 8.6%.

A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 28.5%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 44.3%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 3.6%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 10.5%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 21.1%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 7.3%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 16.5%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 33.2%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 15.8%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 16.2%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 39.7%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 22.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 49.6%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 5.4%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 7.4%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.7%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 7.6%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 19.9%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 4.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 15.0%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 16.3%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 35.4%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 15.8%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 0.7%.

ethnicity_note: Everyone aged 3 or over, by two questions of the 2020 census's extended questionnaire: whether they consider themselves indigenous, by their culture, and whether they consider themselves Afro-Mexican, Black or Afro-descendant. A person may say yes to both, and those who did are shown on their own rather than counted twice. No question asks about mestizo or white ancestry; that share is everyone who said no to both. Estimated by INEGI's expansion factors from a sample of about four million homes, so the Afro-Mexican share differs slightly from the full count's. Identifying as indigenous is much wider than speaking an indigenous language, which the language figure shows. INEGI's coefficient of variation for the indigenous share here is 32.9%.
